problem.statement: How can Harlow lift its operating margin from 1.0% in FY2025 to at least 3.0% by FY2028, within $25M of one-time cost and the $20M FY2026 covenant, and which actions should come first?
problem.decision_maker: CEO, seeking board approval of the margin plan and its first actions
success_criteria: Operating margin of at least 3.0% by FY2028
Operating income of at least $20M in FY2026 (lender covenant)
At most $25M of one-time cost or capital over FY2026–FY2028
No closure of a store with a lease beyond 2027 without a board vote; delivery kept in some form
problem.accuracy: Direction and order of magnitude (about ±20%) on each move; FY2023–25 actuals exact

one_day_answer.situation: Harlow grew sales to $1.50B, but its operating margin fell from 3.4% to 1.0% in two years
one_day_answer.complication: Management blames wages and plans an 8% hours cut, which leaves promotions, shrink and delivery untouched and could raise shrink
one_day_answer.resolution: Cut money-losing promotions, move hours to where shrink is high, reprice delivery and exit loss-making stores as leases end
